newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest direct hogs seen steady-off $1 - dealers.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest direct hogs seen steady-off $1 - dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hogs Thursday were seen selling steady to $1.00 per cwt lower, pressured by weak pork demand and reports of further slaughter reductions, livestock dealers said.
IBP Inc Wednesday said its seven pork plants were reducing operating hours by four to eight hours this week and next due to poor operating margins.

Many meat packers, including IBP, cut slaughter four weeks ago in response to deep losses in margins, but strong cash hog prices linked to relatively tight supplies kept margins in unprofitable territory, sources said.

Cash hog prices rose on Wednesday, with interior Iowa/southern Minnesota top prices on hogs delivered to packing plants up $0.50 at $61.00 per cwt, compared with Tuesday and up $4.00 since prices started their recent climb a week ago, USDA statistics showed.
Interior Iowa and southern Minnesota top prices for hogs delivered to plants Thursday were seen $0.50 to $1.00 lower in a range of $60.00 to $60.50.
Illinois top prices at the plant could range $61.00 to $61.50 and Indiana/Ohio tops could span $60.00 to $61.00.
